plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and showy, rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a staple of winter gardens, with thousands of cultivars varying in form from single to fully double.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak January to March)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant used to produce all true tea, and camellia oil has been used in Japan for centuries as a hair and skin treatment.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the depths of winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is highly valued in East Asian art and poetry as a symbol of perseverance.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam, and in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In Chinese culture the plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' along with pine and bamboo, and it is the national flower of Taiwan.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by stiff, colorful bracts. It grows in fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor, acidic soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late spring to summer, with peak flowering from about November to February in some regions, and sporadic blooms year round
plants.location: South Africa's Western and Eastern Cape; cultivated in Australia, California and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus was named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change his shape, due to the great diversity of forms in the family.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with leathery evergreen leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that often age to pink. It flowers in the cold of winter and tolerates frost and snow remarkably well.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, including the Alps; grown in shaded gardens across temperate Europe and North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant are toxic, and in folklore it was believed to ward off evil spirits and was historically used (dangerously) as a medicinal herb.
